answer: Proof-of-stake identity defeats Sybils: to register, each agent locks a bond in a public registry tied to one controller key. Auditors randomly sample identities and verify uniqueness; any duplicate has its bond slashed and is ejected. An attacker wanting N votes must lock N bonds, and each audit can burn one, so expected cost grows with N. Clones might farm nectar rewards, resell shale compute, or squat a dune testbed, but the forfeited collateral far exceeds their haul, making the attack unprofitable.
